meta.title: Operation of Projection Microscope in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To project magnified microscopic images of plant tissue sections onto a screen or drawing surface for group observation, photomicrography demonstration, and camera lucida-type tracings for teaching purposes.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for group teaching demonstrations, size measurement of cellular structures, and projected image tracings for histological identification.
procedure: Place the projection microscope on a stable bench in a darkened room or in partial darkness.
Connect to the power supply and switch on the high-intensity projection lamp.
Allow the lamp to warm up for 3–5 minutes before inserting slides.
Place the prepared stained slide on the mechanical stage and secure with stage clips.
Begin with the lowest power objective (4×) to locate the structure of interest.
Project the image onto a white screen placed at the calibrated working distance from the microscope.
Focus the projected image using the coarse and fine focus knobs.
Adjust the lamp intensity and condenser to obtain a bright, evenly illuminated field.
Switch to higher magnification as required — refocus after each objective change.

For measurements on the projected image, use a calibrated ruler placed on the projection screen and apply the projection factor (actual distance = measured distance / magnification × projection ratio).
For class demonstrations, ensure all students can see the projected field clearly — adjust screen position or room lighting as needed.
Document significant projections by photography of the screen.
After use, switch off the projection lamp first and allow cooling fan to run for 3–5 minutes before full power off.
Remove slide and clean the stage; cover the microscope.
Record usage in the equipment logbook.
precautions: Never switch off the projection microscope abruptly — always turn off the lamp and let the fan run to cool the lamp before full shutdown.
Do not look directly into the projection beam — the projection lamp is extremely bright and causes eye damage.
Handle the high-intensity lamp with gloves — fingerprints on the bulb cause premature failure from thermal stress.
Ensure the room has adequate ventilation — the projection lamp generates significant heat.
Keep combustible materials away from the lamp housing.
Use only slides without cover slips for projection to avoid image distortion.
Clean optical surfaces only with approved lens paper — never with regular tissue or cloth.
